Q: How can I remove duplicates from a Python list while preserving the original order? A:

The collections module in the standard library provides an OrderedDict which is similar to a normal dictionary but remembers the order in which keys were first added. You can use OrderedDict.fromkeys(...) to create a new OrderedDict from an input list (all values set to None), and then retrieve the keys in the order they were first inserted -- and without any duplicates -- using the keys() method. So:

import collections

def dedup(xs):
    return list(collections.OrderedDict.fromkeys(xs).keys())

should work:

>>> dedup([1,2,2,3,1,4])
[1, 2, 3, 4]
>>> dedup([4,3,3,2,4,1])
[4, 3, 2, 1]

Q: Navigating to page fragment with Javascript A:

Each of the undermentioned perform this function:

  • #!/usr/bin/env xdg-open
location.hash = "fragment";

  • #!/usr/bin/env xdg-open
history.pushState(null, "", "fragment");

  • #!/usr/bin/env xdg-open
history.replaceState(null, "", "#fragment");

  • #!/usr/bin/env xdg-open
document.getElementById("fragment")?.scrollIntoView({
    behavior: "smooth",
    block: "start"
});
